brief.topic: Sahih Muslim 233a: the five prayers and Friday to Friday
brief.audience: Muslims who want a short, trustworthy daily reminder they can act on

coreInsight: Sahih Muslim 233a says the five prayers and one Friday prayer to the next are an expiation for what is between them, if major sins are avoided: each week has a place to return to.

hooks.notes: Warm and short; fits the day.
Relatable, but less tied to Friday.

selectionRationale: Most relevant and clearest at a glance; the teaching pays it off.

scenes.onScreen: It's Friday. Come back. / However this week went.

scenes.purpose: Teaching: the source, verbatim, with its reference.
scenes.kicker: THE MESSENGER OF ALLAH ﷺ SAID

scenes.onScreen: REFLECTION / A weekly return. / This hadith links the five daily prayers and Jumu'ah, week after week. A week of slips doesn't have to keep you away. Turn back to Allah, and come to Jumu'ah today.
body: This hadith links the five daily prayers and Jumu'ah, week after week.
A week of slips doesn't have to keep you away. Turn back to Allah, and come to Jumu'ah today.

caption.opening: Jumu'ah Mubarak. However this week went, today is a day to come back.
body: Sahih Muslim 233a links the five daily prayers and one Friday prayer to the next.
Today: make istighfar for the week behind you, then come to Jumu'ah.

claims.text: Treating each Friday as a weekly return to Allah, with istighfar, is our reflection on the hadith.
